Article Title: Samsung Q2 results: Tech giant posts record high $62 billion profit on AI chip boom
Article Text:
Semiconductor business drives quarter



SK Hynix also posts record revenue, but misses expectations



Heavy investments raise concerns



China’s chip progress weighs on investor sentiment



South Korean chipmakers and AI partnerships



Samsung Q2 results: South Korean technology giant Samsung Electronics has posted its highest-ever quarterly operating profit as the artificial intelligence boom continues to fuel demand for memory chips, especially those used in AI servers.Samsung reported an operating profit of 89.5 trillion won ($62 billion) for the April-June period, marking a more than 19-fold jump from the same period a year earlier. The results came a day after rival SK Hynix also announced record earnings, reflecting the chip industry's strong performance.However, the record numbers could not translate into gains for investors as shares of both companies have declined sharply this week amid concerns over large-scale investments to expand production capacity and growing competition from China.Samsung’s semiconductor division was the main contributor to its second-quarter performance, supported by rising chip prices, increased demand for AI servers and higher shipments of advanced high-bandwidth memory chips used in AI applications.The strong performance of the chip business helped counter an operating loss reported by Samsung’s mobile, television and home appliances division, which was partly impacted by higher component costs.Along with record operating profit, Samsung also reported its highest-ever quarterly revenue at 171.5 trillion won ($119 billion).The company expects demand for its memory products to remain strong in the second half of the year, supported by continued expansion of AI infrastructure and wider adoption of agentic AI.“Demand for server chips is expected to accelerate further, keeping the market undersupplied,” Samsung said in a statement.Samsung’s results followed SK Hynix’s announcement of record second-quarter revenue of 60.5 trillion won ($42 billion). However, even after clocking record-high profits, the figures still fell short of market expectations. The company’s shares fell by more than 9% on Wednesday, while Samsung’s stock also declined during the week.Samsung and SK Hynix together account for about two-thirds of the world’s memory chip production.The two companies have been making major investments in semiconductor manufacturing facilities and data centres as South Korea pushes ahead with its AI expansion plans.While AI demand has boosted the memory chip market, some analysts have expressed concerns about whether the companies’ massive spending plans will deliver sufficient returns.Samsung and SK Hynix announced last month that they would invest a combined 800 trillion won ($554 billion) in a new chipmaking hub in South Korea’s southwest region to capitalise on rising AI-driven demand.Investors have also been closely watching competition from China, which has added pressure on South Korean chipmakers.Concerns among investors increased after reports that a state-owned Chinese company had started mass-producing domestically developed immersion deep-ultraviolet (DUV) lithography machines, a key technology for advanced chip manufacturing.Investor sentiment was also affected by the strong stock market debut of Chinese memory chipmaker ChangXin Memory Technologies, according to some analysts.The developments have added to worries around the future competitive landscape for Samsung and SK Hynix as they continue expanding their semiconductor operations.The push to expand AI-related semiconductor capabilities has also led South Korean technology companies to deepen cooperation with global technology firms.The chiefs of Samsung, SK and South Korean automaker Hyundai joined President Lee Jae Myung during his San Francisco trip last week, where they announced hundreds of billions of dollars in planned cooperation with major US technology companies.The agreements involve AI companies OpenAI and Anthropic, along with chip designers Nvidia and Broadcom, and cover chip technologies, data centres and other AI infrastructure.In a roundtable with foreign media last week, Kim Yong-beom, Lee’s chief policy adviser, said the initiatives show how global technology companies are seeking long-term partnerships with South Korean chipmakers to secure reliable supplies of memory chips for AI.
Article Summary: Samsung reported an operating profit of 89.5 trillion won ($62 billion) for the April-June period, marking a more than 19-fold jump from the same period a year earlier. The results came a day after rival SK Hynix also announced record earnings, reflecting the chip industry's strong performance.

Article Title: Crude prices retreat as oil continues flowing through Hormuz alternatives
Article Text: After a dramatic rally in the previous session, oil prices retreated on Thursday as crude continued to move out of the Middle East even as the US-Iran war widened beyond its primary battlefronts.WTI crude slipped 0.54% to $84.00 a barrel, while Brent crude fell 0.85% to $89.97 a barrel.The decline followed a sharp rebound on Wednesday, when Brent jumped 7.91% and WTI gained 6.56%. The gains had erased the losses from Tuesday, when both benchmarks had dropped about 5% after hostilities briefly paused in the five-month conflict.Even as tensions intensified, shipping activity suggested that oil supplies were still finding routes out of the region. Preliminary data showed 39 commodity vessels entered the Red Sea through the Bab el-Mandeb Strait on Tuesday, the highest number recorded since July 19. Traffic through the Strait of Hormuz, however, remained limited."While overall volumes are reduced, oil continues to leak out of the region through multiple channels, and additional workarounds are being explored. The longer this situation persists, the more these alternative routes and methods will erode Iran's leverage over the Strait of Hormuz," IG market analyst Tony Sycamore said in a note cited by Reuters.The Strait of Hormuz, which previously handled around one-fifth of global oil and gas flows, has remained largely blocked since the US-Iran war began in February, despite diplomatic efforts aimed at reopening the waterway.A senior Iranian official said Tehran had rejected an Omani proposal for regional joint management of the strategic passage.Military action in the region also intensified. US-Saudi strikes targeted Iran-backed paramilitary forces in Iraq on Wednesday, marking the first publicly acknowledged participation by Saudi Arabia in US air strikes. The operation was carried out in response to drone attacks on Saudi oil facilities launched from Iraq.The strikes marked the return of US military action in the Middle East after President Donald Trump halted a bombing campaign over the weekend because of dwindling munitions.Iran said it had responded by firing on US bases in Jordan and attacking three tankers travelling through the Strait of Hormuz, claiming the vessels had used an unauthorised route.Separately, sources said Saudi Arabia was working to assemble a coalition to protect shipping in the Red Sea from Houthi attacks.The Iran-backed Houthi movement in Yemen had announced on July 20 that it would impose a naval blockade on Saudi Arabia in the Red Sea. The group said it would widen attacks on tankers and also target shipping through the Bab el-Mandeb Strait, opening another front in the ongoing Iran war.Meanwhile, though crude prices have once again jumped to the $90 per barrel mark, the spike is still less than the $126 per barrel reached earlier during the conflict.
Article Summary: WTI crude slipped 0.54% to $84.00 a barrel, while Brent crude fell 0.85% to £89.97 a barrel. The decline followed a sharp rebound on Wednesday, when Brent jumped 7.91% and WTI gained 6.56%. The gains had erased the losses from Tuesday, when both benchmarks had dropped about 5%.

Article Title: India-US trade pact: Piyush Goyal explains the one condition to seal the deal
Article Text:
100% tariff threats



The long proposed India-US bilateral trade agreement will enter its first phase only after Washington restores India's tariff competitiveness against rival exporting nations,Addressing concerns around the much awaited trade pact, commerce and industry minister Piyush Goyal on Wednesday, said that the understanding reached between the two countries was based on India receiving a comparative advantage over competing economies, including neighbouring countries and those in the ASEAN region.Once the condition is met again, the agreement would be ready to come into force.Addressing reporters, Goyal said, "I have categorically and on several occasions expressed the confidence that what we have finalized with the US as the first tranche of the bilateral trade agreement, which was announced by our leaders on 3rd of February, will come into operation as soon as the United States is able to ensure that we get a comparative advantage over our competitors, the countries in our neighborhood, the countries in the ASEAN region and other countries with whom we compete. "He added that India is confident of increasing its exports to the US market, provided its tariff treatment is favourable or at par with competing countries."For us, as long as we have comparative advantage or comparable duties, I think India will continue to grow its exports and continue to leverage the large US opportunity," he said.The minister also said India had participated in the Office of the United States Trade Representative's Section 301 investigations related to forced labour concerns.Under that probe, the US has imposed a 10% tariff on India.The minister’s remarks come as attention remains locked on a legislative proposal by the US administration that could allow tariffs to be imposed on countries purchasing Russian energy.The Lindsey O Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act of 2026, introduced in the US Senate, would authorise the US President to impose tariffs of up to 100% on imports from major buyers of Russian crude oil and natural gas.However, the proposed legislation would not automatically result in tariffs.Under Section 113, Trump would have discretionary authority to decide whether tariffs should be imposed, determine the countries that would be covered and fix the applicable tariff rate.The proposal comes at a time when the US-Iran war has disrupted crude oil flows through the Strait of Hormuz. Middle Eastern suppliers, which account for a significant share of India's crude oil imports, have either reduced exports or altered shipping routes.To offset the shortfall, India has increased purchases of Russian crude oil, which was supported in part by the US sanctions waiver, which has since lapsed, although India has continued procuring Russian crude.According to the background information, India's imports of Russian crude reached a record 2.6 million barrels per day in June and are expected to average close to that level during July.On July 28, the US Senate voted 86-12 to invoke cloture, a procedural step that ends debate and allows the legislation to move to a final vote.
Article Summary: commerce and industry minister Piyush Goyal on Wednesday, said that the understanding reached between the two countries was based on India receiving a comparative advantage over competing economies. Once the condition is met again, the agreement would be ready to come into force.

Article Title: US Federal Reserve meet today: Kevin Warsh-led FOMC keeps interest rates unchanged
Article Text:
Inflation has remained above the US Fed's 2% target for more than five years. (AP photo)

Kevin Warsh-led Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) decided to keep the interest rate unchanged in the 3.5-3.75% range. The US Federal Reserve announced the monetary policy review after deliberations on July 28 and July 29."The Committee decided to maintain the target range for the federal funds rate at 3-1/2 to 3-3/4 percent, in support of the Federal Reserve’s dual mandate. The Committee is continuing its policy of maintaining ample reserves in the banking system," the statement read.“Economic activity is expanding at a solid pace despite elevated uncertainty that owes, in part, to the conflict in the Middle East. Productivity growth and capital investment are strong. Job gains have kept pace with the workforce, and the unemployment rate has changed little. Inflation remains elevated relative to the Committee’s 2 percent goal, in part reflecting supply shocks that have driven price increases in certain sectors, including energy,” the statement added.The US Federal Reserve, which began its two-day policy meeting on Tuesday, was widely expected to leave its benchmark interest rate unchanged.Inflation has remained above the US Fed's 2% target for more than five years. Earlier this month, new Federal Reserve Chair Kevin Warsh told Congress that he had “no tolerance’’ for persistently high inflation. This week's meeting is the second monetary policy meeting under his leadership.Oil prices have been highly volatile in recent weeks. Brent crude fell to as low as $72 per barrel earlier this month before surging to $102 last week amid uncertainty over whether the United States and Iran could reach an agreement to restore the free movement of oil tankers through the Middle East.These sharp fluctuations have revived concerns that inflation could accelerate again, just as price pressures had begun easing faster than economists had anticipated.Although higher interest rates help contain inflation, they can also slow economic growth and weigh on stock prices as well as other financial assets.Expensive growth stocks are particularly sensitive to higher borrowing costs, and investors have become increasingly cautious about semiconductor companies and other firms that have benefited from the artificial intelligence boom.Inflation has remained above the Federal Reserve's 2% objective since early 2021, when the US economy rebounded strongly following COVID-19 lockdowns. It peaked at just over 9% in mid-2022 before gradually easing after the Fed raised interest rates 11 times during 2022 and 2023. Since then, however, progress in bringing inflation down has largely stalled.Apart from the conflict involving Iran, inflationary pressures have also been driven by President Donald Trump's tariffs on imported goods and a surge in investment in AI-focused data centres, which has increased demand for computer chips, equipment and electricity.Core inflation, which excludes food and energy prices, moderated in June, partly because rental inflation slowed. A temporary decline in petrol prices during the month also helped keep overall inflation in check.Even so, several Federal Reserve officials have argued that further interest rate increases may be required to bring inflation back to the central bank's 2% target.
Article Summary: The US Federal Reserve decided to keep the interest rate unchanged in the 3.5-3.75% range. Inflation has remained above the US Fed's 2% target for more than five years. Earlier this month, new Federal Reserve Chair Kevin Warsh told Congress that he had “no tolerance’’ for persistently high inflation.

Article Title: Asian stocks trade mixed after Fed holds rates; Kospi rallies 4%, Shenzhen slips 300 points
Article Text: Asian equities showed signs of stabilising on Thursday, but investors remained cautious after a turbulent week marked by a sharp AI-driven market sell-off, uncertainty over the US interest rate outlook and renewed geopolitical tensions that briefly sent oil prices soaring.Taiwan's benchmark climbed 666.47 points to 40,705.65, up 1.66%, while South Korea's Kospi gained 201.22 points to 5,864.46, rising 3.55%. Japan's Nikkei rose 881.37 points to 62,315.56, up 1.43%. Even so, the Nikkei was still headed for a weekly decline of 3%, while the Kospi remained on track for a 12% fall.In Hong Kong, the Hang Seng slipped 34.84 points to 25,773.08, down 0.13% around 8 am IST. In China, Shanghai lost 12.14 points to 3,816.329, down 0.32%, while Shenzhen declined 299.165 points to 13,359.279, falling 2.19%.Elsewhere, Australia's ASX 200 fell 0.48%, Singapore's STI eased 0.64% and Malaysia's benchmark was down 0.15%. New Zealand's NZX 50 dropped 1.43%.The sharp correction in South Korean equities has been at the centre of investor concerns this week after more than $2 trillion was wiped off the country's stock market.The sell-off, concentrated in chipmakers, has fuelled worries over whether the massive investments being made in artificial intelligence will generate adequate returns.The decline was severe enough for Finance Minister Koo Yun-cheol to apologise for the introduction of single-stock leveraged ETFs."Given that the fundamental thesis remains intact, there does appear to be an irrational, panic-like element to the current selling," Gina Kim, portfolio manager for emerging market equities at Nordea Asset Management in Singapore told Reuters."I cannot comment on when the panic will stop as such but some indicators to look out for would be margin balances in both Taiwan and Korea for retail investors. Both are declining but we would ideally need to see some levelling off," said Kim.Samsung Electronics offered some support to market sentiment after reporting a record second-quarter operating profit, up 19-fold from a year earlier.In commodities, Brent crude slipped back below $90 a barrel after jumping more than 7% in the previous session as fighting in the Middle East intensified. Despite continued missile and drone attacks, tanker traffic out of the region has continued, according to available data, easing some immediate supply concerns.The Federal Reserve left interest rates unchanged, but its policy decision did little to settle markets. Instead, the split within the central bank left investors debating whether further rate hikes remain on the table.The uncertainty was reflected in the bond market, where longer-dated treasury yields climbed to their highest levels in 19 years. The 30-year treasury yield stood at 5.2039% after touching 5.2273%, its highest level since June 2007. The dollar also weakened following the policy announcement.At his post-meeting press conference, Fed Chair Kevin Warsh reiterated the central bank's commitment to tackling inflation but refrained from signalling its next move. He pointed to the rise in bond yields since the previous policy meeting, saying markets had already priced in tighter financial conditions, while noting that did not necessarily require the Fed to act.

Article Title: Mahindra arm, SML combine to be 4th largest CV player
Article Text:
Representative image

NEW DELHI: Mahindra Group has outlined an ambitious growth road map for its newly combined truck and bus business, targeting a 10-12% share of India's heavy commercial vehicle (HCV) market by FY31 and over 20% by FY36, as it seeks to strengthen its presence across the commercial vehicle spectrum following the consolidation of Mahindra Truck & Bus Division (MTBD) with SML Mahindra.The combined entity will become India's fourth-largest commercial vehicle player and will focus on intermediate and light commercial vehicles (ICV/LCV), buses and heavy trucks. It will command an estimated 23-24% share in the ICV segment, where the company said it aims to emerge as the industry leader over time. In LCV trucks, the combined share stands at around 13.5%.
Article Summary: Mahindra Group has outlined an ambitious growth road map for its newly combined truck and bus business. The combined entity will become India's fourth-largest commercial vehicle player. It will focus on intermediate and light commercial vehicles (ICV/LCV), buses and heavy trucks.

Article Title: Microsoft Q4 results: Azure tops $100 billion as AI growth helps beat earnings estimates
Article Text:
Azure hits milestone, Copilot adoption expands



Investors look for returns from heavy AI investments



Microsoft’s push into artificial intelligence is beginning to show stronger returns, with the company reporting a sharp rise in cloud revenue and a growing base of paid AI users in its latest quarterly results.The technology giant posted revenue of $90 billion, or $4.81 per share, for the April-June quarter, an 18% increase from the year-ago period. The results exceeded Wall Street expectations, with analysts surveyed by FactSet Research having forecast earnings of $4.24 per share on revenue of $87.62 billion.The company’s cloud business remained a key growth driver, with Microsoft Cloud revenue reaching $59.3 billion during the quarter, up 27% year-on-year. Revenue from Azure and other cloud services rose 43%, reflecting continued demand for Microsoft’s cloud infrastructure, AI applications and services.For the full fiscal year that ended in June, Microsoft recorded revenue of $331.8 billion. Meanwhile, net income climbed 31% to $35.8 billion on a GAAP basis, while diluted earnings per share (EPS) increased 32% to $4.81.Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella highlighted the momentum in the company’s cloud and AI businesses, pointing to milestones achieved during the year.“This year, Azure revenue surpassed $100 billion for the first time, and Microsoft 365 Copilot reached over 30 million paid seats, reflecting the confidence customers are placing in us to power their AI transformation,” CEO Satya Nadella said in a statement Wednesday.The growth of Azure and Copilot together suggests Microsoft is gaining ground by combining AI infrastructure with AI-powered workplace tools, according to Michael J. Wolf, founder and CEO of Activate Consulting.The company is “winning on both fronts,” Wolf said in a statement, adding that Microsoft is “supplying the cloud infrastructure for enterprise AI while monetizing the AI tools embedded in the products workers use every day.”The latest results came at a time when investors have been closely tracking whether Microsoft’s significant AI investments can translate into returns.Azure and Copilot, the company’s flagship AI assistant, have been at the centre of these expectations as concerns over rising AI spending have increased across the industry.Microsoft chief financial officer Amy Hood told investors during a call that the company’s capital expenditure and investment expectations for calendar year 2026 remain unchanged.An accounting change will bring the guidance closer to approximately $175 billion, Hood said, but the actual expectations remain “unchanged”. The move differs from competitors that have continued to increase their spending forecasts.Earlier this year, Hood had said Microsoft expected capital expenditure of $190 billion in 2026, including around $25 billion due to the impact of higher component pricing.Microsoft’s capital expenditure for the latest quarter stood at $41 billion.Bryan Hayes, an investment strategist at Zacks Investment Research, said in a statement that “for the first time in three quarters, the market appears willing to grant that the spending is buying something real.”Microsoft said it remained confident about the longer-term returns from its investments.“We remain very confident in the long-term return on these investments, given these strong demand signals, the increasing product usage we’ve seen and the efficiencies that we’re driving across the platform,” said Danielle Criste, Microsoft's director of investor relations, in an interview.Following the earnings announcement, Microsoft shares rose around 9% to $426.03 in after-hours trading.
Article Summary: Microsoft posts 18% increase in revenue to $90 billion for April-June quarter. Cloud revenue up 27% year-on-year to $59.3 billion. Microsoft 365 Copilot reaches over 30 million paid seats, CEO Satya Nadella says. Microsoft shares rise 9% in after-hours trading.

Article Title: 'GenAI to reshape workforce, GCCs to cushion job impact'
Article Text:
Representative image

BENGALURU: GenAI is poised to transform India's labour market over the next decade, redefine job roles and accelerate the shift towards higher-value work, according to a new Goldman Sachs report.The report estimates that GenAI could automate 9-17% of tasks currently performed by India's non-agricultural workforce. However 8-12% of jobs face a meaningful risk of substitution, while 42-48% are more likely to be augmented by AI, allowing workers to focus on more complex tasks.For India's technology sector, the findings challenge the narrative that AI will sharply reduce employment. While routine coding, software testing, documentation and business process services are increasingly vulnerable to automation, the broader technology ecosystem continues to expand, supported by multinational companies setting up global capability centres (GCCs) and growing demand for digital engineering and AI implementation.GCCs are expected to play a crucial role in cushioning the employment impact. India now hosts 2,117 GCCs generating nearly $98 billion in revenue. The report notes that employment reductions have largely been confined to India's six largest IT services firms, which together cut about 64,000 jobs over the past three years.In contrast, the rest of the technology services industry-including GCCs-added nearly 700,000 employees during the same period, taking the total headcount to about 4.4 million.
Article Summary: GenAI could automate 9-17% of tasks currently performed by India's non- agricultural workforce. 8-12% of jobs face a meaningful risk of substitution, while 42-48% are more likely to be augmented by AI. India now hosts 2,117 GCCs generating nearly $98 billion in revenue.

Article Title: IPL's business value crosses $20 billion, RCB top brand: Report
Article Text:
File photo: RCB

BENGALURU: Indian Premier League 's business value rose 11.4% from a year earlier to $20.6 billion in 2026, helped by growing revenues, digital viewership and record franchise transactions, according to a study by investment bank Houlihan Lokey.It also pegged Royal Challengers Bengaluru's brand value at $312 million, 16% higher than the previous year and making it the first franchise to cross the $300 million mark. Despite finishing ninth in the last season, Mumbai Indians saw its brand value rising 9% to $264 million and was ranked second. This is the second consecutive year in which the league has recorded double-digit growth in business value. Its standalone brand value increased 10.3% to $4.3 billion, adding more than $1.1 billion since 2023. Total league revenues crossed $1.8 billion during the year.Based on media-rights value per match, IPL ranks second globally, behind only US National Football League, the report said.The year also saw two of the league's biggest ownership transactions. RCB was acquired by a consortium of Blackstone, Bolt Ventures, Aditya Birla Group and The Times of India at a reported valuation of just under $1.8 billion. Houlihan Lokey described it as the most expensive transaction involving a single IPL franchise.Rajasthan Royals was acquired by the Mittal family and Adar Poonawalla at a reported valuation of a little less than $1.7 billion. "We were actively engaged in the processes for both RCB and Rajasthan Royals, and both are great assets. Across the league, however, RCB's fanbase intensity and connection are unparalleled, which made this a special opportunity," said Satyan Gajwani, vice-chairman of RCB and chairman Times Internet.The IPL already commands attention comparable to NFL but earns far less from it. As incomes in India rise and connected television reaches more households, its revenues are expected to catch up with its audience scale, Gajwani added."What the market confirmed this year, through landmark franchise transactions, is the extent to which the league can attract precisely the calibre of global, institutional, and strategic capital it was built to draw."Franchise valuations have reached new highs, private capital participation has accelerated, and the league's commercial ecosystem continues to diversify," Harsh Talikoti, director at Houlihan Lokey, said in a statement."Centralised media rights, revenue sharing and financial discipline have created a model that's stable and sustainable. That gives owners the confidence to invest for the long term rather than simply think about the next season," said Ness Wadia, co-owner of Punjab Kings.
Article Summary: Indian Premier League's business value rose 11.4% from a year earlier to $20.6 billion in 2026. Royal Challengers Bengaluru's brand value at $312 million, 16% higher than the previous year. Mumbai Indians saw its brand value rising 9% to $264 million and was ranked second.

Article Title: Smartphone exports rise 23% to $9.8 billion in Q1
Article Text: NEW DELHI: Smartphone exports rose 23.4% to $9.8 billion during the June quarter, with the segment accounting for nearly two-thirds of electronic shipments of about $15.2 billion during April-June.This was the highest-ever first-quarter smartphone exports by value and was driven by strong iPhone shipments to the US, reinforcing the country's emergence as a key global manufacturing hub for Apple.However, industry executives and analysts cautioned that sustaining the momentum through the rest of the year may become more challenging amid slowing global demand, rising component costs and the absence of Apple's upcoming foldable iPhone from Indian production.The US remained the dominant destination, accounting for 71% of India's smartphone export value during April-May, as Apple continued shifting production for the American market to India. Industry estimates suggest smartphone exports could touch $35 billion in FY27, up from $29 billion in FY26, according to industry estimates.Prabhu Ram, VP at CyberMedia Research (CMR), said India's smartphone exports continue to benefit from Apple's manufacturing shift but warned that sustaining growth would depend on global demand.
Article Summary: Smartphone exports rose 23.4% to $9.8 billion during the June quarter. This was the highest-ever first-quarter smartphone exports by value. US remained the dominant destination, accounting for 71% of India's smartphone export value.

Article Title: Exporters flag concerns over West Asia war impact
Article Text:
File photo: Union minister of commerce and industry Piyush Goyal

NEW DELHI: Exporters are worried due to uncertainty of orders, higher logistics costs, liquidity issues and possible disruption of raw material supply chain due to a prolonged crisis in West Asia, with other shipping channel (Bab el-Mandeb) also affected.The issue briefly came up for discussion during a meeting between commerce and industry minister Piyush Goyal and export promotion bodies on Wednesday. While fuel prices have gone up after dipping last month, exporters said they are witnessing delays in execution of orders due to uncertainty in shipping schedules and buyers are adopting a cautious approach, with some seeking extensions in delivery timelines and others delaying fresh purchase decisions. Trade bodies, such as Fieo, are demanding a fresh set of measures to help businesses deal with the crisis, an industry representative present in the meeting said.Another executive said that Goyal received feedback on the situation. During the meeting, he is learnt to have backed further support for service exporters, especially hospitality and medical tourism, a person familiar with the deliberations said.Later, at the JRD Tata Memorial lecture organised by industry body Assocham, Goyal said that the India story has remained resilient despite the global uncertainties."In the first quarter of FY27, war continues. Petrol, crude, gas, diesel, all have all faced uncertainty. Hormuz has been opening and closing through this period. Now we have the Red Sea crisis; it is only expanding. Despite that, as I speak to you today, our merchandise exports have grown by 15% so far in the current fiscal," he said.He also said trust deficit between business and govt has sustained in spite of the several reforms undertaken over the years and asserted that Centre is working to "truly address" the issue, particularly through its efforts to make it easier to do business and reduce compliance burden.
Article Summary: Exporters are worried due to uncertainty of orders, higher logistics costs, liquidity issues and possible disruption of raw material supply chain. The issue briefly came up for discussion during a meeting between commerce and industry minister Piyush Goyal and export promotion bodies on Wednesday.

Article Title: Gold loans rise on larger ticket sizes, unsecured credit shift
Article Text:
Representative image

MUMBAI: Gold loans are surging despite low growth in the number of borrowers as well as the quantity of gold that is pledged with lenders. Gold loans have grown over 50% in FY26 largely because of larger loans by existing borrowers and a shift from other personal loan products to secured gold loans.Gold loans accounted for 22.4% of total consumer credit as of March 2026, making them the second-largest retail credit segment after home loans, which had a 26.3% share. NBFCs increased their share of the organised gold loan market to 22% in March 2026, while gold loans accounted for 20% of their assets under management.According to a study by Icra, growth in the gold loan book over the past five years was primarily driven by rising gold prices. NBFC branch additions and the total tonnage of gold jewellery held as collateral grew at a modest rate of 3-4%, compared to a 24% expansion in the loan book of major players during 2021-22 to 2025-26. Data from credit bureau CRIF reveals that the number of borrowers grew by only 3.1% in FY26 to 899.2 lakh."Growth was achieved via higher collateral valuation per gram, allowing existing borrowers to take higher ticket sizes against the same physical gold," said A M Karthik, senior vice-president and co-group head, financial sector ratings, Icra."Gold loans have functioned countercyclically, capturing demand from borrowers shifting away from unsecured credit options (such as personal loans, SME credit, and microfinance) toward secured gold financing," he added. In other words, existing borrowers are using the gold already pledged with lenders to borrow more.Among nationalised banks, the largest share of gold loans is with Canara Bank, whose non-agri gold loan book crossed Rs 1 lakh crore in Q1FY27. "We expect gold loans to continue growing at a strong pace going forward given the bank's concentration of branches in South India where gold loans are popular," said Brijesh Kumar Singh, the bank's MD and CEO.According to Karthik, the slowdown in unsecured lending had prompted lenders to shift their focus to gold loans.
Article Summary: Gold loans accounted for 22.4% of total consumer credit as of March 2026. The number of borrowers grew by only 3.1% in FY26 to 899.2 lakh. The slowdown in unsecured lending had prompted lenders to shift their focus to gold loans.

Article Title: Banks collected Rs 7,100 crore as ‘minimum balance’ penalty in 2025-26
Article Text:
Minimum balance penalty (representative image)

NEW DELHI: Banks collected nearly Rs 7,100 crore as penalties from customers for failing to maintain minimum average balance (MAB) in their accounts in financial year 2025-26, up from around Rs 6,800 crore in the preceding year, government has told Parliament. Nearly 70% of the charges, adding up to Rs 4,948 crore, were collected by private banks, which saw MAB charges rise by 17% in FY26.HDFC Bank alone collected nearly Rs 1,800 crore, followed by Axis Bank (Rs 1,081 crore). ICICI Bank levied Rs 353 crore, Kotak Mahindra Bank Rs 290 crore, Yes Bank Rs 195 crore and IDBI Bank Rs 175 crore.Govt said that of the 12 public sector banks (PSBs), 10 have discontinued penal charges for non-maintenance of MAB in savings accounts, while two have rationalised it in accordance with their board-approved policies and for commercial considerations.As a result, the 12 PSBs saw a decline in their MAB collections during FY26 to Rs 2,137 crore from Rs 2,775 crore in 2024-25. Among PSBs, State Bank of India (SBI), which levies charges on current accounts, collected Rs 477 crore in FY26, followed by Bank of Baroda (Rs 394 crore), Indian Bank (Rs 299 crore) and Canara Bank (Rs 213 crore).Starting financial year 2021-22, PSBs have collected nearly Rs 12,000 crore as MAB charges.Though data prior to financial year 2022-23 is not maintained for private lenders, they have cumulatively collected around Rs 16,000 crore since then as penalties from customers.“In cases of non-maintenance of the agreed minimum balance in accounts, banks have been advised by RBI to notify customers through SMS, email, letter or other appropriate means. Customers are generally provided time to restore the required minimum balance before penal charges are applied,” said government.
Article Summary: Banks collected nearly Rs 7,100 crore as penalties from customers for failing to maintain minimum average balance (MAB) in their accounts in financial year 2025-26. Nearly 70% of the charges, adding up to Rs 4,948 crore, were collected by private banks, which saw MAB charges rise by 17% in FY26.

Article Title: E20 petrol may harm BS-III vehicle rubber parts, says Nitin Gadkari
Article Text:
File photo: Union minister Nitin Gadkari

No need to modify engines: Gadkari

NEW DELHI: Road transport minister Nitin Gadkari informed Rajya Sabha Wednesday BS-III vehicles, manufactured between 2005 and 2016, may require replacement of some rubber parts and gaskets when run on E20 petrol, while adding studies have found no major impact of the blended fuel on overall vehicle performance.In a reply to a question, Gadkari said studies conducted by IOCL, Indian Institute of Petroleum, Society of Indian Automobile Manufacturers and Automotive Research Association of India (ARAI) found BS-VI vehicles continued to meet emission norms when tested with E20 fuel.Gadkari added studies have not shown any need to modify the car and two-wheeler engines. “These studies confirmed that even legacy vehicles did not exhibit any significant variations in performance, nor do they show abnormal wear-and-tear when operated with E20 fuel. No issues were reported in parameters such as drivability, startability, metal compatibility, and plastic compatibility,” he said.However, the minister said tests on BS-III vehicles manufactured before 2016 indicated that some rubber parts and gaskets may require replacement.TOI on July 7 first reported that an ARAI report, which is yet to be made public, had concluded E20 fuel may damage rubber parts in E10 compliant vehicles.Government has maintained that the loss in mileage depends on factors, including driving habits, maintenance practices such as oil and air-filter changes, tyre pressure, wheel alignment and air-conditioner usage.
Article Summary: Road transport minister Nitin Gadkari informed Rajya Sabha Wednesday BS-III vehicles, manufactured between 2005 and 2016, may require replacement of some rubber parts and gaskets when run on E20 petrol. He added studies have not shown any need to modify the car and two-wheeler engines.

Article Title: Companies boost health cover with top-ups for cancer
Article Text:
Representative image

MUMBAI: Employers are widening employee health benefits beyond conventional group medical insurance as companies seek protection against diseases that can quickly exhaust standard health covers. Reflecting this shift, AstraZeneca Pharma India has become the first company in India to buy a group cancer care policy that sits on top of its existing group health insurance, covering nearly 25,000 employees and their family members.The policy, which has been structured by Howden India Insurance Brokers with a private insurer, supplements, rather than replaces, the employer's base group medical cover.Most companies buy group medical insurance with a sum insured of Rs 3 lakh to Rs 5 lakh, but cancer treatment often costs several times more. The additional cover is designed to meet expenses once the underlying group health policy is exhausted and also pays for certain cancer-related treatments that may not be covered under the base policy."This was a basic need that we identified, and we've been working on it for almost a year to basically thrash out the edges on this product," Amit Agarwal, CEO of Howden India, told TOI. "Although cancer-related treatment is covered under your GMC policy, the insurance limits are pretty less.On average, Indian corporates buy anywhere between Rs 3 lakh to Rs 5 lakh. God forbid, if somebody actually faces a cancer kind of a challenge. These policy limits were not enough." He added that discussions with another 10-12 employers are in the pipeline."Group health, when it started, was taken more as a retention tool by corporates. Today, most of these policies have become a standard inclusion in your package," he said. "Now, what we're seeing is that there is a big trend towards out-patient (OPD) and wellness. If you have 100 employees, only about 9 or 10 will use this medical facility. Whereas OPD would actually be utilised by 50-60% of your population in a year. A lot of these companies are investing heavily in OPD. "Howden spent nearly a year developing the cancer care product with insurers before placing the first policy. Under the structure, companies continue to buy their regular group health policy while deciding how much additional cancer cover they want. Agarwal said the product differs from retail cancer insurance because it has been built for employer-sponsored health plans and covers employees with pre-existing diseases."Most of the cancer products that were available in the market were available on an individual basis," he said. "Because we have made it in a corporate construct, even if you have a pre-existing disease, it gets taken care of." He added that where the base group medical policy excludes certain cancer treatments, "this policy will drop down as well and cover you from ground up.""This is the first of its kind in the Indian market. This product had never been placed in the Indian market," Agarwal said.He said the product would need at least 100 corporate policies and 12 to 24 months of claims experience before its pricing and long-term pricing could be assessed.
Article Summary: AstraZeneca Pharma India has become the first company in India to buy a group cancer care policy that sits on top of its existing group health insurance. The policy, which has been structured by Howden India Insurance Brokers with a private insurer, supplements, rather than replaces, employer's base group medical cover.

Article Title: NEET UG Counselling 2026 to introduce one-time physical reporting, online verification reforms
Article Text:
NEET UG Counselling 2026: MCC introduces student-friendly changes for medical admissions

NEET UG Counselling 2026

:

MCC introduces simplified admission process for candidates



Online resignation, digital verification among key changes



Expanded support for PwBD candidates and cybersecurity measures



NEET UG 2026 counselling support measures



Union Health Minister Jagat Prakash Nadda has reviewed the preparedness for NEET UG Counselling 2026, with the Medical Counselling Committee (MCC) set to introduce several technology-driven reforms aimed at making the medical admission process more transparent and student-friendly.The review covered the readiness of the MCC, Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS) and other stakeholders for counselling under the All India Quota (AIQ) and other seats managed by the committee. Officials presented updates on the counselling schedule, digital infrastructure, cybersecurity measures, grievance redressal systems and candidate support facilities.The NEET UG Counselling 2026 process will feature a one-time physical reporting system to reduce repeated visits by candidates to medical colleges. After seat allotment, candidates will be able to choose between the Freeze and Float options online.Candidates selecting the Freeze option will have to physically report to their allotted institute within the given timeline for completion of admission formalities, including original document verification and fee payment.Those opting for the Float option, which allows participation in further rounds for seat upgradation, will be able to complete admission formalities through online mode.Such candidates will not need to physically report, submit original documents or pay admission fees until they receive a final seat after the permitted upgradation rounds.The upgradation facility will remain available until the third round of counselling. After the third round, candidates with allotted seats will need to report physically to their respective institutions for final verification and admission completion.Another major change introduced for NEET UG Counselling 2026 is the online resignation facility. Candidates permitted to resign from their allotted seats under applicable rules will be able to submit requests through the MCC Counselling Portal without visiting the institute, unless otherwise specified.The counselling process will also include pre-populated candidate data from the National Testing Agency (NTA), online document verification, seat matrix validation by the National Medical Commission (NMC), and verification by participating institutions.The admission process for NRI candidates will also be fully digitised. Applicants will upload required documents through the counselling portal, which will then be verified online by designated officials. The move replaces the earlier document submission process through email.The Health Ministry has expanded facilities for Persons with Benchmark Disabilities (PwBD) candidates by increasing the number of designated assessment centres from 16 to 61 across the country.Under revised guidelines issued by the National Medical Commission, the disability certificate for admission assessment will now be referred to as the "Eligibility Certificate". The guidelines aim to create a uniform and evidence-based assessment framework for PwBD candidates.An Appellate Disability Assessment Board will also allow eligible candidates to appeal against assessments conducted by the initial disability assessment board.The ministry said cybersecurity preparedness for the counselling process has been reviewed in coordination with the National Informatics Centre (NIC). Training programmes have also been conducted for disability assessment boards, college nodal officers and document verification officers.To assist candidates, MCC has established a 24×7 toll-free helpline and introduced bilingual information material, frequently asked questions and guidance videos. A dedicated grievance redressal mechanism has also been created for resolving candidate queries.The National Testing Agency declared the NEET (UG) 2026 results on July 16, 2026. Counselling for MBBS, BDS and BSc (Hons.) Nursing seats under the All India Quota is expected to begin shortly.Candidates have been advised to read the counselling scheme, information bulletin and applicable rules carefully before making choices related to seat acceptance, upgrades, resignation or disability assessment.
Article Summary: Medical Counselling Committee (MCC) set to introduce several technology-driven reforms aimed at making the medical admission process more transparent and student-friendly. The NEET UG Counselling 2026 process will feature a one-time physical reporting system to reduce repeated visits by candidates to medical colleges. Online resignation, digital verification and expanded support for PwBD candidates among key changes.

Article Title: Voting begins for Bankipur, Datia and Manjalpur assembly bypolls
Article Text:
(With agency inputs)





PATNA: Voting began on Thursday for by-elections in the Bankipur assembly constituency in Bihar, Datia in Madhya Pradesh, and Manjalpur in Gujarat.Polling is underway at designated booths across the three states, with the counting of votes scheduled for August 3.In Patna, BJP MP Vivek Thakur and senior party leader CP Thakur cast their votes at the Bihar State Library polling station on Dak Bungalow Chauraha Road, located in the Bankipur assembly constituency.After casting his vote, Vivek Thakur expressed confidence in a decisive victory for the BJP in Bankipur."In Bankipur, the Bharatiya Janata Party is moving towards a landslide victory. There is enthusiasm among people. And after the passing of yesterday's bill, the youth across the country are once again united, as they have always been with the Bharatiya Janata Party. Because of the scene in the House yesterday, those who were creating obstacles were the Congress Party and Rahul Gandhi. It's their advisors who have come to Patna to contest elections. So no one is going to be misled; there will be a landslide victory," Vivek told ANI.When asked if he would return to Parliament, Vivek Thakur said, "I'm going. Off to Delhi."CP Thakur said his entire family had voted and expressed confidence in a "landslide victory" for the party they support."With the whole family. We all help the party we support; the whole family votes for that party. Landslide victory," he said."This is a changed Patna. We have been voting at this booth for the last 30 years," CP Thakur added.Polling also began for the Manjalpur by-election in Vadodara, Gujarat, while voters queued up at designated polling stations in Datia, Madhya Pradesh, for the assembly bypoll.The Bankipur assembly seat fell vacant after BJP leader Nitin Nabin resigned as MLA following his election to the Rajya Sabha. Nabin had won the constituency in the 2025 assembly elections, defeating RJD candidate Rekha Kumari by a margin of 51,936 votes.The BJP has fielded Neeraj Kumar Sinha as its candidate for the Bankipur bypoll. Former Bihar chief minister and JD(U) MP Nitish Kumar had urged voters to support Sinha, saying every vote was crucial to maintaining the pace of development in the state.BJP national president Nitin Nabin also appealed to voters to back the NDA candidate, describing Sinha as a dedicated party worker who had risen through the organisational ranks.Meanwhile, Bihar Leader of Opposition and RJD leader Tejashwi Yadav expressed confidence in winning the Bankipur by-election. "We are clearly going to win the election..." Yadav told ANI.In Madhya Pradesh, the Datia assembly seat fell vacant after Congress MLA Rajendra Bharti was disqualified on April 2 under the provisions of the Representation of the People Act, 1951.The BJP has fielded Ashutosh Tiwari, while the Congress has nominated Ghanshyam Singh for the Datia bypoll.Tiwari replaced former Madhya Pradesh home minister Narottam Mishra as the BJP candidate. Mishra had represented Datia for three consecutive terms from 2008 to 2018 but lost the seat in the 2023 Assembly elections.The Manjalpur seat in Gujarat fell vacant following the demise of sitting BJP MLA Yogeshbhai Narandas Patel.
Article Summary: Voting began on Thursday for by-elections in the Bankipur assembly constituency in Bihar, Datia in Madhya Pradesh, and Manjalpur in Gujarat. Polling is underway at designated booths across the three states, with the counting of votes scheduled for August 3. Bihar Leader of Opposition and RJD leader Tejashwi Yadav expressed confidence in winning the bypoll.

Article Title: Before the knowledge walks out the door
Article Text:
Everyone in Silicon Valley is racing to build machines that replace human expertise.

Ahmer Inam

, a schoolteacher's son from Delhi, is building machines that inherit it.

When Ahmer Inam appeared on Fox & Friends in June, his mother watched the segment without following much of it. Her English is limited. There was her son on the famous curved couch of American morning television, fielding questions about artificial intelligence, and she understood almost none of the words. She wept anyway. Some distances need no translation, and the one between a schoolteacher's household in Delhi and a Manhattan television studio is legible in any language.Had she followed the argument, it might have surprised her less than it surprised the audience. Because what Inam was defending, underneath the vocabulary of frontier AI, is approximately the oldest idea in civilisation — the one his father practised for a living: that knowledge survives only when one generation troubles to hand it to the next.Inam has spent twenty-five years building artificial intelligence — long enough to remember when it meant symbolic logic in the late nineties, and senior enough to have run AI and data for Fortune 500 companies, Nike and Wells Fargo among them, back when "chief AI officer" was still an exotic title. He is not, in other words, a critic sniping from the cheap seats. Which makes the thesis of Cognisee, the research lab he founded and leads, sound almost seditious in today's Silicon Valley: "We're not trying to replace the worker," he says."We're trying to make the worker irreplaceable."The problem he is aiming at usually gets filed under the bland heading of "labour shortage." By one estimate, more than two million skilled-trade jobs in the United States could sit unfilled by 2030 — electricians, welders, machinists, the hands America needs if it is serious about building factories, chip plants and grid capacity again. But Inam's diagnosis is sharper than a headcount. "America does not have a work shortage," he likes to say. "It has an expertise shortage."Consider what actually leaves the building when a master electrician retires at sixty-eight. Not the manual — the manual stays. What leaves is the ear that catches a motor running slightly wrong two weeks before it fails; the instinct that connects a faint vibration to a pattern in old maintenance logs; forty years of judgment that was never written down because it could not be. The philosopher Michael Polanyi had a name for this — tacit knowledge, the things we know but cannot tell — and Cognisee is, at bottom, a bet that the most valuable training data on earth is tacit.The company's method has a fable-like symmetry. Its AI begins as an apprentice: it works alongside experienced people and learns what they notice, what they ask, how they make judgment calls. Then it turns around and becomes a coach, carrying that accumulated judgment to the newcomer. "First it's an apprentice," Inam says. "Then it becomes a coach." Picture a 22-year-old on his first aircraft-maintenance job, hearing a sound he has never heard before, with the distilled instincts of the country's best technicians beside him in real time. "He's not being replaced by a machine," Inam says. "He's being mentored by one."The repository where all this lives is called, a little grandly, a Wisdom Vault — a secure library of hard-won know-how from doctors, nurses, electricians, factory workers, farmers, small-business owners. Grand or not, the name gives away the emotional register Inam is working in. This is not pitched as workforce optimisation. It is pitched as inheritance.He is careful — insistent, actually — about the question that framing invites: who owns it? In Cognisee's design, the expert decides what to preserve, what to share, and with whom; the contributor is recognised and rewarded; the knowledge belongs to the person who earned it, not to the machine that absorbed it. "There is a big difference," Inam says, "between being monitored and being mentored." The company is incorporated as a public benefit corporation, which he describes as a legal commitment to the worker rather than a marketing pledge.That ownership principle is also where his quarrel with the reigning AI paradigm becomes explicit. The frontier labs, Inam argues, got intelligent by swallowing the written internet — and the written internet is now substantially swallowed, which is why the industry's plan increasingly amounts to bigger data centres and more electricity, even as some of the field's own pioneers warn of a wall ahead. His contrarian wager is that the next leap will come not from more compute but from the knowledge that never made it onto the internet in the first place — and that it can be gathered by consent rather than by crawler.For an Indian reader, the resonance is hard to miss. This is a country that has watched its weaves, its remedies and its craft knowledge catalogued, carried off and sold back to it before. It is also a country whose deepest teaching traditions were never textual at all, but moved from person to person — the guru-shishya parampara, the ustad and the shagird. Inam has spoken about Wisdom Vaults for indigenous and medicinal knowledge, with communities retaining ownership of what they contribute. One way to describe Cognisee is as an attempt to give the world's oral inheritances an infrastructure layer — sovereignty included.The idea is attracting converts from unexpected quarters. Cognisee's co-founder, Alex Giannou, spent nearly two decades on Wall Street financing precisely the data centres and power deals behind the AI boom; he crossed over, in Inam's telling, because the right bet and the smart bet turned out to be the same one. Among the company's early backers is a senior Google executive who helped invent federated learning, one of the foundational privacy-preserving techniques of modern machine learning. And last year the XPRIZE Foundation, where Inam serves as a Visionary, recognised his work with its Global Visioneering Award.None of which quite explains the conviction. For that you have to go back to Delhi. Inam grew up in a low-income household, the son of a teacher — a man who spent his working life on the least scalable expertise-transfer technology ever devised: one adult, one room, one generation at a time. The son's journey to America was not gilded; there were stretches, early on, when he could not always afford to eat. It takes a particular kind of person to emerge from that and conclude that a nation's most undervalued asset sits not in its server farms but in the heads of its retiring machinists and nurses."Every generation should start where the last one left off," Inam says. It sounds like a product principle. It is closer to a family creed — the thing his father practised without ever calling it a thesis, the thing his mother recognised on a television screen in a language she does not speak. Some knowledge, it turns out, transfers just fine.
Article Summary: Ahmer Inam, a schoolteacher's son from Delhi, is building machines that inherit it. The problem he is aiming at usually gets filed under the bland heading of "labour shortage" By one estimate, more than two million skilled-trade jobs in the United States could sit unfilled by 2030.

Article Title: EU's new salary transparency rules: 'Pay has long been treated as deeply personal'
Article Text:
The law behind the numbers

Not just a gender story

The hardest part isn't the spreadsheet

Your compensation model defines the workforce you attract

Why the law alone won't close the gap

Losse's real fix: Three things, not one

Across the European Union, women earn on average 11.1% less per hour than men. In India, government figures show male salaried workers earning roughly 24% more than their female counterparts. In the United States, women took home about 85 cents for every dollar men earned in 2024, per the Pew Research Center.The comparative numbers explain why a new EU law is being watched well beyond Europe. For decades, the gap has persisted partly because pay was rarely open to scrutiny; what colleagues earned, and why, stayed behind closed doors. That is about to change in Europe, where a sweeping new regulation is forcing companies to open their books on who earns what, and why.At its core, the directive is designed to make it harder for pay inequity to hide in plain sight. Its stated goal is to strengthen the principle of equal pay for equal work, or work of equal value, by giving employees the information and legal standing to check whether their own pay is fair.Formally Directive requires companies across the European Union's 27 member states to disclose pay ranges to job applicants, ban questions about salary history, and give employees the right to ask what colleagues doing equal work earn.Larger employers must also publish gender pay gap data every one to three years, and build a “job evaluation” system, using objective, gender-neutral criteria such as skill, responsibility, effort and working conditions, that explains why one role pays more than another. Where the unexplained gap within a job category exceeds 5%, employers must address it, with worker representatives, within six months.Member states were required to transpose the directive into national law by June 7, 2026. By that deadline, according to law firm trackers, only a handful of countries, among them Italy and Slovakia, had full implementing legislation in force. Economies including Germany, France, Spain, Austria and the Netherlands had missed it outright, with Brussels signalling that infringement proceedings could follow.When Tanja Losse and her team at Eurogroup Consulting ran a full job evaluation across a European financial services firm's workforce earlier this year, benchmarking every role against the market and against internal peers doing comparable work, the results surprised her. A significant share of employees, considerably more than her client had anticipated, turned out to be paid less than their role and level warranted, not because anyone had deliberately shortchanged them, but because, in many cases, nobody had ever formally checked.“Pay has historically been treated as something deeply personal, almost taboo to discuss,” explains Losse, a strategy consultant for financial services at Eurogroup Consulting who has spent much of the past year helping European banks prepare for a new EU regulation whose implications reach well beyond compliance and into business strategy. “In practice, what someone ends up earning has often come down to how well they negotiated, rather than the role itself or how they perform in it. ”Losse's case findings complicate the assumption that pay inequity is simply a story about women being underpaid relative to men. Among the employees she identified as underpaid, the split between men and women was close to even, roughly half and half. What differed was the size of the gap: among underpaid women, the shortfall relative to what their role warranted was consistently larger than among underpaid men, even though similar numbers of each were affected. “It tells you this isn't purely a gender issue, it's a negotiation and structural issue that happens to hit women harder,” Losse notes.Losse says the technical side of a project like this, pulling the data, running the job evaluation, is the easier half. What decides whether it actually works is who backs it and how carefully the result gets delivered. In her experience, that means keeping the chief executive close with regular updates, and treating the works council and the company's controlling function as partners rather than checkboxes to clear.The group most often overlooked, she says, is the one with the most at stake: the employees themselves, some of whom fear the audit will mean they end up earning less. That is why she treats the communication around a project like this as being just as important as the analysis itself.One discovery from her most recent project reshaped how her team ran it. The leadership team turned out to be far less consistent than expected: some managers held regular, structured conversations with their staff about performance, others held almost none. That gap mattered because those same managers would have to deliver the audit's most sensitive finding directly to each employee, which pay bracket they now sat in, and what their development path looked like from there.Losse's team responded by building a dedicated coaching programme to prepare managers for those conversations, including the pushback some were likely to face. She now treats how well a leadership team handles that individual conversation as one of the clearest predictors of whether a pay equity project succeeds or quietly fails. The measurable result, she says, was a completely rebuilt compensation framework, covering salary and every other monetary benefit, delivered within a year, an ambitious timeline for an organisation of that size and complexity.On paper, implementing a regulation like this can look like a purely technical exercise: pull the pay data, run the numbers, file the report. Losse pushes back on that framing. In her experience, it is at its core a change and communication programme, one that ends up shaping the workforce a company will have five or ten years from now, including who it keeps, who it promotes and who it can attract in the first place.“People treat this as a data or IT migration project. It isn't. It's setting the path for the workforce you want to keep, promote and attract,” Losse insists.That strategic weight shows up most clearly in how a compensation model actually gets designed, she says. Fairness demands rules that apply uniformly, the same bonus structure for everyone in a given role, for instance, so pay cannot simply come down to who negotiates hardest. But a model built only on uniform rules risks flattening the one thing that keeps ambitious employees engaged: a visible path for growth.The harder design problem, in her view, is building in enough structure to guarantee fairness while leaving room for a development track that rewards learning and growth, and enough flexibility to retain or reward the highest performers. “If you make it completely rigid, you lose the ability to develop and motivate people, and you risk losing your high potentials. If you make it too flexible, you're back to the same inconsistency the law is trying to fix. Getting that balance right is the hardest part of the whole design,” she adds.That, she contends, is why the exercise is worth doing even for companies outside the EU with no legal obligation to run one. The underlying questions, how to define fair pay, how to keep a visible development path open, and how to stay flexible enough to compete for talent, are workforce strategy questions every company eventually has to answer, regulation or not.That question already has an answer, of sorts, in parts of the world with no EU-style mandate. In the United States, roughly 19 states, including California, Colorado, New York and Illinois, require salary ranges in job postings, but there is no federal law and no single national standard. India's Code on Wages, 2019, already requires equal pay for equal work, but it carries no requirement to disclose pay data or ranges, leaving enforcement to inspection and individual complaint rather than routine transparency.Even full compliance, Losse argues, will not by itself close Europe's pay gap. The directive addresses pay gaps within a given role or job level; it does little about the fact that women remain underrepresented in the highest-paid roles in the first place, a pattern researchers call occupational segregation.The 2025 Women in the Workplace report found that for every 100 men promoted to manager, only 89 white women and 54 Black women received the same promotion, a bottleneck at the first rung of management, not the top, that compounds over a career.Losse points to two structural levers she considers more consequential than transparency law alone: childcare and reskilling. Affordable, accessible childcare, she argues, determines whether women can stay on a career track at all, rather than trading progression for flexibility.And as generative AI reshapes which roles survive, employers need to actively invest in moving workers out of the roles most exposed to automation and into higher-value, higher-paid ones. Research led by Stanford economist Erik Brynjolfsson found that employment for early-career workers, ages 22 to 25, in the most AI-exposed occupations has fallen roughly 13% since 2022, even as employment for older workers in the same fields grew, a divergence that has held for nearly four years with no sign of reversing.“If we don't actively help people in at-risk roles move up the skills ladder, transparency on today's pay structure won't matter much, because the structure itself is about to shift,” Losse says.Losse's bottom line is less about any single law than about sequencing. Pay transparency, she says, is a genuinely useful first step: it forces companies to justify pay decisions they may never have examined, and it takes the negotiation advantage away from whoever is simply better at asking. But on its own, it will not close a gap rooted as much in who gets promoted and who can afford to stay in the workforce as in what any individual is paid for a given role.“Transparency, childcare access and a genuine commitment to reskilling, those three things together are what actually move the number,” she concludes.For Losse, the interest is not purely professional. Financial literacy has mattered to her since early in her career, when she volunteered teaching children about money, and giving people a fair, transparent stake in their own finances is a large part of what drives her.It is also why she pays close attention to research like Brynjolfsson's: the question she thinks companies and employees now have to answer together is which skills, among them leadership, empathy, communication and the ability to keep learning, will keep a workforce relevant as AI reshapes which jobs remain.(Tanja Losse is a strategy consultant for financial services at Eurogroup Consulting, where she advises banks on strategy, transformation and organisational change.)
Article Summary: Women earn on average 11.1% less per hour than men in the European Union. In India, government figures show male salaried workers earning roughly 24% more than their female counterparts. In the United States, women took home about 85 cents for every dollar men earned in 2024.

Article Title: Oil prices jump over 7% as Middle East chaos flares up, brent crude back at $90 per barrel
Article Text: Oil prices rallied sharply on Wednesday, with benchmark crude contracts gaining over 7%, after a fresh wave of military action in the Middle East reignited concerns over global oil supplies. The rally was also supported by industry data showing a drawdown in US crude inventories.Around 9 pm IST, Brent crude rose $6.28, or 7.47%, to $90.37 a barrel, while US West Texas Intermediate (WTI) gained $5.67, or 7.15%, to $84.93 a barrel.The latest jump followed renewed strikes involving the United States, Saudi Arabia and Iran-backed groups, reversing expectations that the US-Israeli war with Iran could soon move towards a resolution."Renewed military strikes in the Middle East and Iranian officials reiterating that they want to control shipping activity through the Strait of Hormuz amid depressed oil flows through the Strait are lifting oil prices again," UBS analyst Giovanni Staunovo told Reuters.The United States and Saudi Arabia carried out strikes on Iran-backed groups in Iraq on Wednesday, saying the groups were responsible for drone attacks on Saudi oil facilities.Earlier, the US military said that it had prevented what it described as a surprise Iranian attack on American troops in the region. Iran, in turn, said it had targeted ships in the Strait of Hormuz and US bases in Jordan.Markets found further support after US President Donald Trump said in an interview with Fox News that the United States would respond with retaliatory strikes against Iran.The developments also dealt a blow to diplomatic efforts around the Strait of Hormuz. A senior Iranian official told Reuters that Tehran had rejected Oman's proposal for regional joint management of the strategic waterway, dimming hopes of resolving a months-long impasse that has disrupted Gulf trade.The disruption has continued to affect shipping. Only a small number of commodity vessels have crossed the Strait of Hormuz this week. By comparison, traffic through the Bab el-Mandeb Strait increased, with five ships passing through on Wednesday and 39 on Tuesday, the highest daily count since July 19, before Yemen's Iran-backed Houthi militants announced a maritime blockade of Saudi Arabia.According to regional sources cited by Reuters, the Houthis are also considering imposing charges on commercial vessels using the southern Red Sea. Six sources familiar with the matter also said China has held direct discussions with the group to ensure its oil tankers can transit the route without being attacked.Analysts said oil prices are likely to remain volatile as the conflict continues to shift."We believe Brent oil prices will continue to whipsaw in the $80-$100 per barrel range in the near term as the conflict ebbs and flows in the Middle East," said Suvro Sarkar, head of energy research at DBS Bank."The situation has escalated since US President Donald Trump signalled a return to diplomacy earlier in the week," he said."This series of stop-start negotiations means a complete removal of the Strait of Hormuz blockade is not achieved, and oil prices could see higher floor of around $80 per barrel even under a de-escalation scenario."Apart from geopolitical tensions, traders also drew support from inventory data. Market sources, citing figures from the American Petroleum Institute, said US crude stockpiles declined by about 3.3 million barrels during the week ended July 24. Official figures from the Energy Information Administration are expected later on Wednesday.
Article Summary: Brent crude rose $6.28, or 7.47%, to $90.37 a barrel, while US West Texas Intermediate (WTI) gained 7.15, to $84.93 a barrel. The latest jump followed renewed strikes involving the United States, Saudi Arabia and Iran-backed groups.

Article Title: US stock market today: Wall Street in red ahead of US Federal Reserve policy review; oil prices climb
Article Text:
Technology stocks, particularly companies viewed as richly valued, remain under pressure.

US stock market today: US equities traded in negative on Wednesday as investors awaited the outcome of the Federal Reserve's latest policy meeting on interest rates. Meanwhile, oil prices climbed sharply.S&P 500 edged down 0.73%. The Dow Jones Industrial Average lost over 700 points, or 1.42%, while the Nasdaq Composite managed a also dropped 1.05%The biggest moves were seen in the energy market. Brent crude surged 5.6% to $86.64 a barrel after fresh hostilities involving Iran heightened concerns over global oil supplies. Iran launched a missile attack on US forces in the Middle East, while US forces, alongside Saudi Arabia, carried out strikes on Iran-backed militias in Iraq.Oil prices have been highly volatile in recent weeks. Brent crude had fallen to around $72 a barrel earlier this month before briefly touching $102 last week as uncertainty persisted over whether Washington and Tehran could reach an agreement that would allow oil shipments from the Middle East to resume without disruption.The renewed rise in crude prices has fuelled concerns that inflation could accelerate again after showing signs of easing faster than expected.That uncertainty has also complicated expectations ahead of the Federal Reserve's interest rate decision following the conclusion of its two-day policy meeting, according to an AP report.Markets are currently assigning about a 36% probability to a US rate hike, which, if delivered, would mark the first increase in three years. While higher interest rates help curb inflation, they can also dampen economic activity and weigh on equity valuations.Technology stocks, particularly companies viewed as richly valued, remain under pressure. Investors have become increasingly cautious about semiconductor manufacturers and other beneficiaries of the artificial intelligence boom, amid concerns that the rapid pace of earnings growth may not be sustainable if AI fails to deliver the expected gains in profitability and productivity.The shift in sentiment was especially evident in South Korea, where the stock market is heavily influenced by Samsung Electronics and SK Hynix. The KOSPI index fell another 6% after plunging 10.8% in the previous session, reducing its gains for the year to 34.4%.SK Hynix shares dropped 9.6%. Although the company reported record quarterly revenue and profit driven by strong AI-related demand, its 257% revenue growth still failed to meet analysts' expectations.Elsewhere, global markets presented a mixed picture. Hong Kong's Hang Seng index advanced 2%, while France's CAC 40 declined 0.7%.In the bond market, US Treasury yields moved slightly higher alongside rising oil prices. The yield on the benchmark 10-year Treasury note inched up to 4.62% from 4.61% at Tuesday's close.
Article Summary: S&P 500 edged down 0.73%. Dow Jones Industrial Average lost over 700 points, or 1.42%. Nasdaq Composite managed a also dropped 1.05%. Brent crude surged 5.6% to $86.64 a barrel after fresh hostilities involving Iran.

Article Title: South Korea's Kospi tumbles 6% as SK Hynix slide, AI spending worries trigger chip selloff
Article Text:
A screen shows the Korea Composite Stock Price Index (KOSPI) at the Korea Exchange in Seoul, South Korea, Wednesday, July 29, 2026. (AP Photo)

South Korea's benchmark Kospi index plunged 6% on Wednesday, dragged down by a sharp selloff in chipmakers after SK Hynix reported quarterly earnings that, despite surging nearly sixfold from a year ago, missed analysts' expectations.The benchmark index had fallen more than 8 per cent during intraday trade before recovering some losses to close at 5,663.24, its lowest level since early April. The decline came just days after the Kospi had climbed above the 9,000 mark.Shares of memory chip giant SK Hynix tumbled 9.4 per cent after its operating profit for the latest quarter fell short of market forecasts. Samsung Electronics also lost 4.8 per cent, adding to pressure on the index.The selloff reflects renewed investor concerns over lofty valuations of artificial intelligence-linked stocks, particularly semiconductor companies that have been among the biggest beneficiaries of the AI boom.Markets have been hit by repeated bouts of profit-taking in AI-related shares amid growing doubts over whether massive investments in artificial intelligence will generate the expected returns.Investor sentiment has also been dented by China's progress in developing lower-cost advanced AI models, raising concerns over future demand and profitability for premium chipmakers.The weakness spread across the region, with Japan's Nikkei 225 falling 1.5 per cent as chip equipment maker Tokyo Electron slumped 10.6 per cent and Lasertec Corp. dropped 8.3 per cent. Taiwan's Taiex also declined 3.8 per cent.Broader Asian markets were mixed. Hong Kong's Hang Seng gained 1.8 per cent, while China's Shanghai Composite rose 0.4 per cent. Australia's S&P/ASX 200 advanced 1% after inflation data eased concerns over further interest-rate hikes, and India's Sensex traded 1.1 per cent higher.On Wall Street overnight, the tech-heavy Nasdaq Composite slipped 0.2 per cent as AI-related stocks remained under pressure. Micron Technology fell 8.9 per cent, while Advanced Micro Devices and Applied Materials dropped 8.1 per cent and 7.8 per cent, respectively, reflecting continued investor caution toward semiconductor stocks despite generally strong corporate earnings.
Article Summary: The benchmark index had fallen more than 8 per cent during intraday trade before recovering some losses to close at 5,663.24.
